core_obligations: Reduce the fpqc sheaf condition to the case of a Zariski covering together with a covering given by a single faithfully flat ring map, and recall the Zariski case (proof lines 654-660).

Set-theoretic step: for a morphism from the spectrum of the faithfully flat extension whose two pullbacks to the tensor square agree, obtain a map on the underlying sets of the base by descent for maps of sets, and deduce its continuity from the quotient topology statement and continuity of the given morphism (proof lines 662-671).

Localisation step: choose an affine formal open subscheme containing the image of a point, choose a standard affine open neighbourhood of that point mapping into it, and translate the restriction of the morphism into a continuous ring map from the coordinate ring of the subscheme into a localisation of the extension, whose two localisations agree by hypothesis (proof lines 673-684).

Algebraic step: use the equalizer statement for the faithfully flat localisation to factor that ring map uniquely through a ring map into the localisation of the base, note that it is continuous because it has the same open kernel, and obtain a morphism on the chosen open (proof lines 684-692).

Supply the verification that the morphisms constructed on the members of the chosen open cover glue to a morphism from the spectrum of the base, which the author declines to give here (proof lines 694-700).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to a faithfully flat covering (proof lines 654-660).
Descent of the underlying map of sets, and its continuity (proof lines 662-671).
Localisation to a standard affine open (proof lines 673-684).
Descent of the ring map and construction of the local morphism (proof lines 684-692).
Glueing, left to the reader (proof lines 694-700).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the functor of points of a formal scheme satisfies the sheaf condition for fpqc coverings (statement lines 646-652). The proof reduces the topology to the case of a Zariski covering together with a covering by a single faithfully flat ring map, and uses that the sheaf condition for Zariski coverings was already observed when the functor of points was introduced (proof lines 654-660). The substance is the descent of a morphism along a faithfully flat ring map, and it is carried out in three steps. First, a morphism from the spectrum of the faithfully flat extension whose two pullbacks to the tensor square agree is shown to come from a set-theoretic map on the base, by a descent statement for maps of sets; continuity of that map is then deduced from the corresponding quotient topology statement and continuity of the given morphism (proof lines 662-671). Second, the problem is localised: an affine formal open subscheme containing the image of a chosen point is selected, a standard affine open neighbourhood of the point on which the image stays inside that subscheme is chosen, and the restriction of the morphism above it is converted into a continuous ring map into a localisation of the extension, whose two further localisations agree by hypothesis (proof lines 673-684). Third, the ring map is descended: since the localisation of the faithfully flat extension is still faithfully flat, the equalizer statement for a faithfully flat ring map identifies the fixed ring, so the ring map factors uniquely through a ring map to the localisation of the base, which has the same open kernel and hence is continuous, and therefore defines a morphism on the chosen open (proof lines 684-692). The conclusion that the local morphisms glue is left to the reader (proof lines 694-700). The claim is H2: one descent argument is carried through three stages -- set-theoretic, topological and algebraic -- and each stage is displayed, with the single omitted step being the routine glueing of morphisms that have already been constructed locally.
